study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Kim et al., Nature Mental Health, 2024
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Mapping cerebellar anatomical heterogeneity in mental and neurological illnesses

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study used the PCNtoolkit package (version 0.24) to estimate normative models using Bayesian linear regression with likelihood warping approach, specifically using the 'sinarcsinsh' transformation. This approach is designed for handling nonlinear basis functions and non-Gaussian predictive distributions for large datasets.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: We used the PCNtoolkit package (version 0.24) in Python 3.8 to estimate a normative model for predicting regional cerebellar volumes and voxel-wise intensity on the basis of sex and age, while correcting for scanning site. We employed a Bayesian linear regression with likelihood warping approach, specifically using the 'sinarcsinsh' transformation.

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: The study modeled two types of cerebellar morphology measures: (1) lobular volumes (28 cerebellar lobules including bilateral lobules I-VI, crus I and II, lobules VIIB, VIIIA, VIIIB, IX-X, vermis VI-X, and corpus medullare) using the ACAPULCO algorithm, and (2) voxel-wise gray matter probability values (multiplied by the Jacobian of the transformation matrix to preserve volumetric information after normalization) using the SUIT toolbox, resulting in approximately 143,000 voxel-wise models.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: Cerebellar morphology was quantified as lobular volumes or voxel-wise gray matter probability values (multiplied by the Jacobian of the transformation matrix to preserve volumetric information after normalization... The algorithm divides the cerebellum into 28 cerebellar lobules... In addition, the gray matter maps were modulated by the Jacobian to preserve the value of each voxel in proportion to its original volume.

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: The normative models included age and sex as covariates, while controlling for scanning-site-related variability. Scanning site was treated as a fixed effect in the analysis.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: All normative models included age and sex as covariates, while controlling for scanning-site-related variability... We used the PCNtoolkit package (version 0.24) in Python 3.8 to estimate a normative model for predicting regional cerebellar volumes and voxel-wise intensity on the basis of sex and age, while correcting for scanning site... To account for scanner effects, we treated the scanning site as a fixed effect in our analysis.
